When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training years ago and I started with MMA. It was my passion and I knew I wanted to train this.

Training: I train mostly twice a day and it is a regular daily routine for a fighter. 

What professional titles have you held? I was champion of TFL (Thunderstrike Fighting League) in the light heavyweight category

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? I didn’t lose a single amateur fight, 18-0

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? Brown belt in BJJ

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? The fight with Caio Borralho on 04/29/2023 was very difficult; my health condition was poor

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Cain Velasquez because he never gave up and always moved forward and was making pressure

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? Yes, my biggest hero is Łukasz Ciepliński. He was a Polish soldier who lived during World War II. I admire the kind of man he was.

Is there a cause you want to use your platform for? Yes, my mission is to promote Polish tradition and history on the international stage.

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? My biggest motivation is my wife and children, and of course my country.

Personal Life / Background: I'm a normal guy who raises two daughters with a loving wife. In my free time, I like to go fishing, and after fishing, I am very interested in historical books. Additionally, whenever I have free time, I try to help my parents work on the farm.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started in 2012. I was finished with football at Northwood University. I went to a WEC event to watch a high school teammate / friend, Dominick Cruz, fight. That was my first exposure to MMA. I was still needing competition after football and I was hooked after that event.
What ranks and titles have you held? WKC (World Karate Commission) National and World gold medal 2019.
Do you have any heroes? My dad. I didn’t like a lot of the rules and parenting growing up and I’m sure I made it difficult, but he stayed on me and made me who I am now. I consider him my best friend now and he’s the best man at my upcoming wedding.
What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means that I’ve accomplished a goal that’s been in the works for close to 10 years. It means the start of a new set of goals that includes financial security for myself and my family.
Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Northwood University – MBA after undergrad
What was your job before you started fighting? Investigator for an insurance company. Responsible for various fraud investigations from fake injuries, staged accidents, ambulance chasing attorneys / medical providers, arson, theft, etc.
Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? Win over Khaos Williams (now a teammate)
Ranks in any martial arts styles: Brown belt in Go-Ti (Karate)
Favorite grappling technique: Ground and pound
Favorite Striking technique: Right hand

Who is your favorite fighter and why? My favorite fighters are Anderson Silva and Jon Jones. They are the greatest role models in fighting for me!

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? Yes, I do! It's Marinho Rocha, a great friend who helped me a lot!

I have been fighting for this for over 13 years and I went through many things to get to the UFC and fulfill my dream. This means a lot because I fought a lot for it, and I know I can be the showman of the UFC. Soon I will be the UFC champion and the showman of the event. I am here to show the fans and the UFC my style of fighting.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I was 20 years old and had never heard of MMA/BJJ or any martial arts disciplines aside from in movies, but on youtube one day i stumbled across a trending video of this woman who of course we all know (but I didn't at the time) - Ronda Rousey. I saw her fighting and demolishing these other women, with a physique not too dissimilar to mine and all I could think of was all those fights I used to get into from when I was a tiny child to high school aged and realised like WHOA - THIS IS AN ACTUAL SPORT!?? So I googled "MMA gym near me", there was one 45mins away called Core MMA (in the same city I was training rugby every day) and I met Carlo that next day and 10 years later, here we are! 

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? 2022 IBJJF Blue Belt Open World Champion, 2021 Shuriken Featherweight Champion, 2020 IMMAF Lightweight Oceania Champion, 2020 + 2019 NZ Submission Grappling National Champion, 2019 IMMAF Lightweight World Champion, 2019 IMMAF Lightweight Oceania Champion, 2019 UWW Wrestling Worlds - NZ Team Member, 2017 Oceania Wrestling Champion

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? Purple Belt in BJJ

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? Abby Montes at Madison Square Garden for sure! I was well prepared but was deaf in there and got way too into a box-off with a big strong Mexican boxer haha which was addicting but not the game plan. Took me until the 3rd round to switch up, get the takedown and secure the RNC. 155lb is fun and all, but that's like my walk around weight and I felt it in that fight more than any other, Abby is an athletic UNIT haha but we had a laugh over a beer about it all after the fight!

Who is your favorite fighter and why? I have a few in mind, but I will go with the current standout in my mind and that's gotta be Diego Lopes. His style in and out of the cage, his quiet and humble confidence, and his striking is amazing but his grappling flow and smoothness flowing between positions and attacking so many different submissions is just beauuuutiful! I remember his first fight short notice against the badass Evleov from ATT (the guy I see doing literal finger tip jumping push ups haha) and man.. that fight just blew my mind with what Diego was doing, and all factors considered too.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? No, I did a one year diploma at the Bay of Plenty Polytechnic in tourism/business. Which led me to a 1 year lifeguarding gig in Florida at the ripe old age of 19 and if I look back at all the dots lining up - it ultimately led me back to American Top Team all those years later!

What was your job before you started fighting? Helped on the farm growing up, did life-guarding for a number of years, and then I spent most of my time as the Factory Manager for Viking Kayaks (this was our family business for 20 years) where we manufactured the worlds best fishing kayaks at the time from little ole Matamata, New Zealand!

Origin of nickname: Since I was able to walk and talk I have been a crazy kid with a "you can't tell me what to do" attitude (for better or worse) and my parents used to call me Wild Child since I can remember! Whether I was picking fights with my big brother or kids at school, or riding the cows and calves on the farm rodeo style while mum and dad were milking, or drifting the home made go-kart down the gravel track on the farm or playing rugby with the boys since 4 years old; the list is endless... The Wild One nickname really needed no second thoughts as far as we all were concerned haha.

Personal Life/Background (family stuff, kids, etc): No kids for me at this stage and I am one of 2 kids myself. Proud aunty to my brother and cousins children though! I grew up on a 300 cow dairy farm, would go possum hunting with my Dad and brother Friday nights and save the babies to take care of and raise (to my Dads quiet dismay i'm sure). My Mum always had a horse or two as she competed in dressage competitions and she grew up riding them in the South Australia outback. I raced BMX for a while alongside my brother and Dad, and my brother and I even competed at the World Championships when they were held in Adelaide, Australia. I grew up on the water too, from fishing off kayaks, boats or rocks, and surfing with my family at the local beaches. We would take our motorbikes on trail rides in the bush and mud whenever we could. Whenever we had a birthday growing up, it would just be 20 kids each riding their own motorbike around the farm, making jumps etc. I got into a little trouble at school - being a bit eager to talk, I'll just say.. And getting into little stupid fist fights probably because of my big mouth too, because I thought I could back it up and shouldn't take shit from anyone - it is safe to say I matured past this and found my way to understanding more of the thoughtful/verbal conflict resolution skills haha.

Who are 3 people you'd love to meet or work with (celebrities, content creators, other fighters, sports stars)?:

  • Cowboy Cerrone - I want to test my bull riding skills against him because I rate myself on the mechanical version..... and race/ride dirtbikes and rally cars with him
  • Travis Pastrana - Always loved this dude growing up, met him once at Nitro Circus and I truly think he could get me to backflip my bike into his foam pit in 1 day for sure.
  • Sallie Grace - she is an adrenaline junkie like me and grew up around boys, motorbikes and hectic activities. Would be a blast and probably wild a heck haha

What are your hobbies, activities or other interests when not training for a fight?: Fishing. Shark tooth hunting. Surfing. Skating/Bike riding. Dogs. DIY / building projects. Country line dancing. Making seashell art/jewelry. Wild life adventuring. Dirtbikes. Rodeo/bull riding. Rugby.

The Ultimate Fighter season 18 coach. Purple belt in BJJ

What was your job before you started fighting? I was working at Costco

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? 5-1 as an amateur

TRAINING:  A typical day of training is never typical. The only thing that I work on every day is wrestling, as it is always incorporated in my training regimen. Everything else is a different story. Since the fight can go anywhere and anything can happen, I work on all aspects of mixed martial arts, where boxing, jiu-jitsu, wrestling, conditioning, kickboxing is all worked on throughout the week, as well as sparring.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started martial arts when I was only seven years old. The training was great and I fell in love with the idea of combat and competition. When I turned nine, my parents could not afford the lessons anymore so I was put in soccer by my dad.  At fourteen, I started to take kickboxing lessons from a local gym and paid for it with money I made doing landscaping work. Kickboxing gave me a good base for my stand-up but at school when I fought with my friends who wrestled, I never did well when the fight hit the floor. Finally at eighteen, my good friend introduced me to a man who taught Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.  After that, everything fell into place with my fight career.  Paying for college with my fight purses, I made sure that I fought at least four to five times a semester. I graduated and figured out that I made more money teaching and fighting so I decided to make it my life.

What ranks and titles do you have? Former WEC Bantamweight Champion. Black belt in BJJ under Carlson Gracie. Total Fight Challenge, Iron Heart Crown, Shooto Americas 132-pound, Extreme Shootfighting, and Superbrawl Champion.  Black Belt in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.

Do you have any heroes? Yes, my father, for always being there for me and teaching me the value of hard work and dedication.

What is you favorite technique?  I love the art of knocking someone out. If MMA was not around, I would be a pro boxer. On the ground I like the arm triangle, I can set it up from so many different positions.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? For me, being able to fight in the UFC is a lifelong dream. I've watched the UFC since the very first show and to be a part of it now is an honor. I always trained my hardest, but all the experiences I've had in the past, combined with my newfound wisdom and great team will guide me down the right path in my walk with the UFC.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to Purdue University and earned a degree in Marketing.

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked in a hospital as a Radiologist’s assistant for five years. Perfect job for a fighter.

When and why did you start training for fighting? Aside from wrestling as a kid, I started training Jiu-Jitsu a few years back in Chattanooga, TN. I was mainly interested in the self-defense aspect of it. I have two young daughters, Bianca 3 and Brea 1, so my number one goal was to be able to defend them if anything were to happen. Unlike most sport jiu-jitsu schools, we spent a lot of time dealing with real life situations such as being attacked by knife or gun.  After a year or so, some of the guys I knew were moving into the MMA game and asked if I would help them train.  I realized through their training that I was giving them a harder time than most of their opponents at much higher weights, so I decided to give it a try. Now I train at Triton CCSD in Tulsa, OK under Piet Wilhelm, which has helped me grow into the fighter I am today.

What ranks and titles have you held? It has been very hard to get any title fights here in the midwest; however, I have had 10 fights (7 as a pro) and have yet to lose, defeating two title holders in non-title fights along the way. I was also ranked the #1 all-round rollerblader in the world for 6 out of the 10 years I skated. I have 2 gold medals, 4 silver medals, and 3 bronze medals from the ESPN X-Games Series. I was a member of the gold medal winning USA Global X-Games. I also won the bronze medal in the NBC Gravity Games. I was named skater of the year in 2002 by the ASA. I have also been featured in magazines such as ESPN the Magazine, Men's Health, Men's Journal, and was voted one of the "Ten Hottest Men in Sports" by Women's Sports Illustrated in 2001.

Do you have any heroes? It wasn’t until I was a father that I had any idea what I must have put my mom through!!! So she will always be my hero.

What is your favorite technique? Any and all chokes.

What does it mean for you to fight in the WEC? It is a dream come true. I love what they have done for the promotion of the lighter weights. I think it is the most exciting fighting out there.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? After high school I went to a number of schools, but I followed my dreams of being a professional skater out to California.

What was your job before you started fighting? I was and still am the Director of Operations / General Manager of the Platinum Fitness Center in Tulsa, OK.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training in 2004.  I had retired from powerlifting at the age of 22 after taking 3rd in the world in my weight class. I was looking for something to do that was competitive and helped pass the time.  My friends were going to an MMA class and asked if I wanted to tag along, so I did.  I literally had no fight training at all, and after getting my butt kicked that night, I told myself I would keep going back until I’d evened the score. Ten weeks later I was running classes and have been in-love with the sport ever since.

What ranks and titles have you held? Currently the number 2 fighter @ 170 in New England. Reality Fighting Welterweight champion

Do you have any heroes? My mother. Never in my life have I seen anyone struggle so much and overcome so much adversity…with a smile.  At times I’ve sat at the dinner table and asked my mother why she wasn’t eating and she said she wasn’t hungry, when in fact we didn’t have enough money or food for her to eat at all.  My mother is a strong independent person and always told me to finish what I start.

What is your favorite technique? Conditioning!!! You can have all the tools in the world, but if you’re not conditioned well enough to perform the task at hand….game over!!!

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? No degree

What was your job before you started fighting? Certified Strength and Conditioning Coach, Certified Personal Trainer - both certifications are through the NSCA.

Most memorable professional fight? Danillo Vilefort...it was my first WEC fight and I lost.  I learned more from that loss than any win and now everyone needs to watch out because it motivated the hell out of me.  Losing Sucks!

What was your most challenging professional fight? My first MMA fight.  I was really nervous and did not know what to expect

Did you compete in any other sport(s) at college or professional level? I competed in professional powerlifting and took 3rd in the world at 198lbs

Who were your training partners for this fight? Marcus Davis, Kenny Florian, Greg Rebello, Matt Phinney and all the guys at Sit Yod Tong and Tim Burrill Jiu Jitsu

What is your favorite thing about this sport? Getting paid to do something I love

How long do you see yourself staying in this sport? Until the fire and desire to compete dies down...that will never happen

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training boxing when I was 14. I was in 9th grade and I was tiny. I was about 5'1" and I got picked on every day for being so small... It sucked, so I took up boxing. Not to fight anyone, But so everyone knew I could fight and would leave me alone. AND IT WORKED. So I boxed for 1 year, gained knowledge out of Cus D'Amato’s, learning from the same man who taught Mike Tyson himself, Kevin Rooney. After a year, I started getting into wrestling, I joined the wrestling team at my school and went 21-3 my first year of wrestling. Now, I was confident in both and I started training MMA at a local lodge where people just met up to practice moves they learned on YouTube. I took my first fight at 16 and it was for a title. I won a hard fight by decision and now I was hooked.

What ranks and titles have you held? 155lb Lightweight Champion of Breakthrough 15 MMA, 155lb Lightweight Champion of Cage Wars, 155lb Lightweight Champion of Kaged Kombat, 155lb Lightweight Champion of Hero Fight League, 2009 N.Y. State Shooto Champion

Do you have any heroes? My mother and father

What would it mean for you to fight in the UFC? EVERYTHING. MMA saved my life. It brought me happiness and with it I can bring happiness to my family. My mother, struggling with 4 kids, I CAN STOP THAT STRUGGLE. I WILL STOP THAT STRUGGLE. She deserves that. When I am in the UFC, I can take away all the pain of struggling in my remaining family. Nothing will stop me from achieving this.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I attended Colombia Greene Community college and received an Associate’s degree in Exercise Physiology

What was your job before you started fighting? I started fighting at 16 and before fighting I worked at Pomodoro’s, an Italian restaurant in my home city...I was a dish washer.

Favorite grappling technique: De la Riva, guillotine, heel hook, wrist lock

Favorite Striking technique: Question mark kick, slip jab, body-head hook, bolo punch, foot movement

What was your job before you started fighting? I was on the world-class program for the U.K. wrestling team leading up to the London Olympics in 2012, but I always helped my dad doing ground work to get the extra money. 
Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? 6-0 amateur record
Ranks in any martial arts styles: European & British jiu-jitsu champion, Commonwealth medalist 2014 in freestyle wrestling

Favorite Striking technique: Body kick
